front, spelled as in the photo ("200 CARTRIGES / 7.62 MM, M108 / CARTONS • M31"). I read the worn "M 08" as M108.
- **Joints:** every part touches or enters the one it attaches to. I checked this numerically and by looking at close renders of all 24 joints.

**Material:** a single olive-drab painted steel. Paint, rust (heavy on edges, the lid border and the hardware), dark worn patches, run-off streaks and the worn stencil are all layers baked into colour, roughness and normal maps. The colours were sampled from the photo.

**Comparison with the photo:** I measured it against the photo four times (two correction rounds as planned, plus a first and a final pass). The final measure, on the shipped file, gives a silhouette overlap of 0.88.
- **Lower half reads up to 39% wider:** this is from the photo's close, high camera, which narrows its base. I didn't distort the model to copy that.
- **Still different from the photo:** the photo's front face is darker and blotchier, its stencil more broken up, and its lid top greener.

**Assumptions:**
- **Size:** you didn't give one, so I used a standard 7.62 mm ammo can. Overall it measures 0.305 × 0.119 × 0.204 m (the body alone is 0.280 × 0.113 × 0.170 m).
- **Invented parts:** the photo shows only one view. The second lid hook on the back is mirrored from the visible one, and the hinge barrel on the far end is made up.

**Things to know about the final file:**
- Your engine needs a Draco decoder and WebP texture support (`EXT_texture_webp`) to load it.
- The compressed normal map lost most of its fine surface relief. `ammo-box_original.glb` (6.5 MB, 2048 textures) keeps it, if you'd rather ship that.

Blender also left an automatic backup, `ammo-box.blend1`. Compact storage normally keeps only the four files below, so I can delete it if you like.
